page: Amazon Web Services c8gb.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features 64 dedicated physical cores running at 2.8 GHz on the 64-bit ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 CPU microarchitecture without simultaneous multithreading (1 thread per core). The instance is configured with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 compute-optimized ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include integrated local storage or dedicated hardware GPU accelerators, but it provides a 133 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark results demonstrate high multi-core throughput and strong memory subsystems. The instance places in the top tier for Geekbench multi-core performance (25,948.0) and Clang software compilation (81,860.0), supported by uncached read memory bandwidth reaching 466.21 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 210.01 GB/sec. Data processing tasks scale well across all 64 cores, reflected in top-tier results for multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (669.84 GB/sec), PassMark database operations (47,513.78), and Redis SET operations reaching 133.04 million ops/sec. Single-threaded performance lands in the middle tier, with stress-ng single-core scoring 1,706.49 and Geekbench single-core at 1,890.0.

The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM balance combined with dedicated physical cores delivers cost-effective compute scaling for parallelized computational tasks, though workloads requiring heavy single-thread speeds or substantial RAM per core face limitations. Lacking local storage, it relies entirely on networked storage volumes. The configuration is optimal for distributed build farms, CI/CD pipelines, containerized microservices, high-throughput web serving, and parallel computational processing.
description: Amazon Web Services c8gb.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the 64-bit ARMv9 AWS Neoverse-V2 processor on the Nitro System. It provides 64 dedicated physical cores at 2.8 GHz, 128.0 GB of memory (2.0 GB per core), and a baseline network bandwidth of 133 Gbps. The instance includes neither local NVMe storage nor GPU accelerators. Benchmark evaluations show top-tier multi-threaded execution and memory bandwidth, scoring 25,948.0 in Geekbench multi-core and 81,860.0 in Clang software compilation, alongside high-throughput results in PassMark database operations and Redis SET operations (133.04 million ops/sec). However, single-core benchmarks remain in the middle 50% band. Given its 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio, the instance is structurally suited for CPU-bound parallel workloads, code compilation, CI/CD pipelines, distributed container clusters, and high-concurrency web serving.
